resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (CCO) for change in ownership
resale_co.lead_time: Contact the Zoning Officer two weeks before closing. By code, the Zoning Officer inspects within 14 days of notice and issues the certificate within one business day of a passed inspection.
requirements: Notify the Zoning Officer of the impending change in ownership and pay the inspection fee
Inspection for obvious noncompliance with Township Board of Health ordinances, Chapter 135 (Sewers) and the Zoning chapter
Smoke and carbon monoxide alarms in the right locations and working at the time of inspection (the CCO fee includes the smoke/CO inspection)
Fire extinguisher (the Township's Smoke & Carbon Monoxide Detectors & Fire Extinguishers handout is linked from the CCO section) (form still lists it)
The inspection does not cover the septic, sewage disposal, well, plumbing, electric or other systems

fees.label: CCO inspection (includes smoke and CO alarm inspection)
fees.quote: The fee is $75.00 checks made payable to the Township of Holland.

fees.label: Second inspection

fees.label: Certificate of occupancy first inspection fee (Code Chapter 83)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Call the Zoning Officer about two weeks before closing to arrange the inspection, and pay $75.00 by check payable to the Township of Holland. The Zoning Officer may ask for an application form. Township offices are at 61 Church Road, Milford, NJ 08848.

evidence.quote: Holland Township requires that you obtain a Continued Certificate of Occupany (CCO) prior to selling, renting or buying a home.
Please contact the Zoning Officer TWO weeks prior to closing to arrange for an inspection.
No Attempt will be made by this inspection to examine the Septic, Sewage Disposal, Well, Plumbing, Electric, or other systems of the property or the construction of any structure on it.
Such certificate shall be obtained prior to the closing of title on any such change of ownership and prior to any actual change in tenancy of the affected building.
The foregoing fee shall include an inspection as to a smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm where such devices are required by state law.
The Tax Search Officer of this Township shall provide a notice of this certificate of occupancy requirement on all issued tax searches for residential property in the Township.

resale_co.notes: Holland Township Code Chapter 115 (read in full through the ecode360 page) requires a certificate of occupancy for any existing 1 or 2 dwelling-unit home on a change in ownership, obtained before closing of title. The Zoning Officer inspects for obvious noncompliance with Board of Health ordinances, the Sewers chapter and Zoning. The Township page calls it a Continued Certificate of Occupancy (CCO) and says the $75.00 fee covers the inspection; Code Chapter 83 also sets $75 for the first inspection and $75 for a reinspection. No phone, email or name for the Zoning Officer is posted on the Zoning page; the Township's online directory lists the Municipal Clerk at 908-995-4847, ext. 210 (Clerk@hollandtownship.org) and the Land Use Board at 908-995-0057. Construction permits are handled by the NJ DCA Bureau of Code Enforcement in Asbury, (908) 713-0722.

Confirm with the Township first, since its CCO inspection already covers smoke and CO alarms.

fire_cert.notes: Holland is State-enforced for the fire code (LEA code S in the July 2026 registry), and the state directory lists the NJ Division of Fire Safety for smoke detector compliance. But the Township's own code says the CCO fee includes the smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm inspection, and the Zoning page lists smoke/CO alarms and fire extinguishers as items checked at the CCO inspection. In practice the Township CCO inspection seems to cover the alarms; whether a separate State certificate is also needed should be confirmed. The linked handout (Smoke-Carbon.pdf) is a scanned image, so its contents could not be read. The fire extinguisher is still listed by the Township even though the state dropped it from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19). Update: the current state fees are $45 / $90 / $161, set by N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) (50 N.J.R. 729(a)) (more than 10, 4 to 10, and under 4 business days before closing). The $35 / $70 / $125 on the older DCA paper form are out of date.

other_items.label: Tax search notice
other_items.detail: The Tax Search Officer puts a notice of the CCO requirement on every tax search for residential property, so the CCO shows up in title work.

open_questions: What is the Zoning Officer's direct phone and email for scheduling the CCO? None is posted on the Zoning page.
Does the Township CCO inspection fully replace the State smoke/CO certificate, or does the State (DCA) also need to issue one?
Does Holland still require a fire extinguisher at resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
How long is the CCO valid after it is issued?
